key_insight: For high-wavenumber Helmholtz problems in 2D and 3D, optimal full-space and truncated UPML inf-sup estimates scale as k⁻¹, enabling preasymptotic error analysis of linear CIP-FEM.
engineering_relevance: These results strengthen the mathematical basis for high-frequency wave simulations using absorbing layers and stabilized finite elements.
method: Establish wavenumber-explicit stability for full-space uniaxial perfectly matched layers.
Transfer optimal stability estimates to the truncated UPML problem.
Derive preasymptotic error estimates for linear continuous interior penalty FEM.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions and demonstrate CIP-FEM effectiveness at high wavenumbers; the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The stability theory requires sufficiently large wavenumbers and specified regularity, piecewise-power structure, and small-absorption derivative bounds for the UPML absorption profile.
paper_title: Optimal stability estimates and preasymptotic error analysis of the CIP-FEM for the Helmholtz equation with uniaxial perfectly matched layers
